analysis.title: Data Insights: Institutions Remain Cautious on Stocks, but Underlying Signals Turn More Supportive
key_insights: Institutional sentiment (relative bullish vs bearish views) and interest (absolute engagement) on KOSPI both fell below average alongside a c.19% local-currency decline from Oct 1 to Oct 27, as concerns over AI infrastructure spending and elevated valuations resurfaced.
Historically, KOSPI's below-average sentiment and interest setup has been followed by 20-day returns of 1.8% vs 1.5% on average, with a 61% probability of a positive return vs 56% on average.

The KOSPI setup is less constructive near term: 10-day volatility has historically run above average (6% vs 5%). JPM Strategists stay cautious until KOSPI shows signs of deceleration in key support zones (Feb-Oct pattern lows). The conditions have not emerged despite an earnings-driven rebound of about 7% on Oct 28, so volatility in the AI/semis trade may persist.

SPX institutional sentiment has dropped below average going into Q3 reporting season despite a supportive earnings backdrop, while institutional interest is rising into a catalyst-heavy week (about 44% of S&P 500 companies reporting, plus the Fed and key US macro releases).

The sentiment/interest setup for SPX has historically been associated with broadly average 20-day forward returns. Sector breadth is more constructive: 8 of 11 sectors have positive month-to-date returns and outperform SPX, while XLK is about 3% lower, leaving room for a recovery in a key SPX driver.

US retail sentiment is close to year-to-date lows with broad weakness across defensives, cyclicals and tech. Past troughs in retail sentiment have often coincided with market rebounds, and JPM is watching for stabilization.

Institutional mentions of French government bonds (OATs) are easing from multi-year highs while the 10Y OAT yield is little changed (4.9%, about -10bps since Moody's affirmed France's sovereign credit). JPM reads this as markets becoming more used to the fiscal and political backdrop, and will watch for a sustained easing in attention as a sign of stabilisation.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield barely moved while institutional attention to OATs eased from multi-year highs, which suggests fiscal and political concerns are largely priced in.

tension_points.bull_case: Below-average institutional sentiment and interest have historically preceded positive 20-day returns (1.8% vs 1.5% average) with a 61% hit rate vs 56%.
tension_points.bear_case: 10-day volatility historically runs above average (6% vs 5%), and JPM Strategists remain cautious until KOSPI decelerates at key support zones. The +7% Oct 28 rebound has not produced that.
tension_points.what_invalidates: KOSPI failing to show deceleration at the Feb-Oct pattern lows (key support zones).
